reading.title: Choosing the Right Size
reading.purpose: Find out why designers pick big or small sizes for the things they make.
paras: Size matters when people design things. A builder thinks about how much room a family needs. An engineer thinks about how a machine will fit where it must go. Even a toy maker has to choose a size.

Some things are made to be huge. A bridge may be gigantic, because it must carry thousands of cars each day. A skyscraper can be so towering that it seems to touch the clouds. A cargo ship is massive, so heavy and solid that tugboats must guide it into the harbor. The ocean it crosses is immense, so wide that sailors can lose sight of land.

Other things are made small on purpose. A model maker builds a miniature train, a tiny copy that fits on a shelf. A camping tent is compact, so it folds neatly and takes little room in a backpack. A bulky sleeping bag is warm, but it is hard to fit into a small pack.

Designers also think about the people who will use a space. A spacious classroom has lots of room, so students can move around. A cramped room has too little space, and the desks bump into one another. A slender bookshelf, long and narrow, can fit in a hallway where a wide one cannot.
Big or small, a good design matches the size to the job.

choices: an old train kept for display in a museum
a train built for very long trips
a tiny copy of a real train
a train too heavy to move at all
qs.why: The words after it explain it: a miniature train is "a tiny copy that fits on a shelf."

qs.q: Which sentence tells why a slender bookshelf is useful?
choices: A slender bookshelf, long and narrow, can fit in a hallway where a wide one cannot.
A spacious classroom has lots of room, so students can move around.
A cramped room has too little space, and the desks bump into one another.
Even a toy maker has to choose a size.
qs.why: This sentence says that a long, narrow shelf fits in a hallway where a wide shelf does not.

ev.text: A slender bookshelf, long and narrow, can fit in a hallway where a wide one cannot.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Bigger things are always better than smaller things in every design.
Only builders and engineers ever need to think about the size of things.
Small things are the hardest to design because they weigh so little.
Good designers match the size of a thing to the job it must do.
qs.why: Every paragraph shows a job that needs a big or small size, and the last sentence says to match the size to the job.

qs.q: Why might a hiker choose a compact tent?
choices: It is heavy and solid, so it stays put in a strong wind.
It folds up small, so it is easy to carry in a pack.
It is spacious enough for a whole class to sleep inside.
It looks like a miniature house, so it is fun to set up.
qs.why: The reading says a compact tent folds neatly and takes little room in a backpack, which helps a person who has to carry it.
